content.content:
1	# Growth — dedup local packs against the canon (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile this repo's **local packs** against the shared **canon** it
4	consumes (Claudinite, vendored read-only), pruning local items — a pack's prose line, or a whole local check —
5	the canon now covers. It opens a PR against the repo's default branch for the owner to approve. Often there's
6	nothing to prune, and that's fine. You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue, whose
7	**Context** is **binding scope — not a hint** (the executor will not let you re-decide or widen it).
8	
9	> This task only prunes local packs against the canon; lifting local items up into the canon is the central
10	> promote task's job (canon-side).
11	
12	## Conventions used in this doc
13	
14	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
15	- **GitHub access is MCP-native.** Updating the tracking issue and opening the PR go through the session's
16	  **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub access — the shell reaches
17	  only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so never reach for `gh`/`curl` or
18	  a cross-repo clone.
19	- **The mounted canon.** The exact canon revision this repo currently consumes — compare against *that*, not a
20	  live fetch. It is what `.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp (a promotion is visible here only
21	  once baselining has converged the mount to include it). Prune only against what the repo actually mounts.
22	- **The dispatch's Context narrows the *yardstick*, never the local surface.** When the Context names
23	  newly-changed canon packs ("Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs: …"), **those packs
24	  are this run's entire yardstick**: every prune must cite a line or rule id from one of *them*, and you never
25	  widen the comparison to the rest of the mounted canon. What is *not* narrowed is the local side — **every**
26	  local item is in play against those packs, whatever it is about. (Local pack names are unrelated to canon
27	  pack names, so there is nothing to match up.) A dispatch with **no** Context block carries no such bound: the
28	  precondition emits the list only when the mounted canon moved, and its other arm — the repo's own local packs
29	  changed — deliberately emits none, so that run compares the fresh local items against the whole mounted canon.
30	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) —
31	  everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the
32	  rename window). That's the corpus this task prunes within; the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under
33	  `.claudinite/` is never a prune target, only the yardstick you prune *against*.
34	
35	## What it does: prune / rephrase local packs the canon now covers
36	
37	When the canon has **absorbed** a practice a local doc still carries — most often an item the central promote
38	task lifted up and the canon now owns — the local copy is redundant. This task:
39	
40	- **Removes** the now-duplicated local item, since the canon is the single source of truth for portable rules.
41	- **Strips** a *partially* covered item down to its residue — when an item's general half is now canon-owned
42	  but it still carries a stronger point about a narrower case, **delete the portable half in place and keep
43	  only the residue**. A strip is a **deletion that shrinks the entry**: lead with the residual point (using the
44	  file's own `(canon)` tag convention if it has one), never with a meta-line like "this rule is portable
45	  (canon)", and **never re-state the now-canon rule, its fix, or which pack owns it** — carrying it is exactly
46	  what you are removing. If your "strip" adds words or restates the canon, you have *un*-deduped the item: keep
47	  the pre-edit text instead.
48	- **Rephrases** a local procedure *only* when the canon's wording of the same idea has changed, so the local
49	  packs stay consistent with the canon they point at — a rephrase tracks a wording drift; it never grows the
50	  entry and never re-imports canon prose.
51	
52	**Keep a local item only if it says *more* than the canon — not merely says it more specifically.** Every
53	local item is more specific than the canon, so specificity alone is never the test. Distinguish two cases:
54	
55	- **The general rule in local dress** — it makes the canon's point but leans on this repo's classes, files, or
56	  names to make it. Once the canon covers the point, those names were only illustration: prune it.
57	- **A stronger point about a narrower case** — it asserts something the canon's general rule leaves out: a
58	  tighter constraint, a sharper claim that holds for this repo's narrower situation. Keep it.
59	
60	So ask not "is it specific" (it always is) but "does it only lean on specific names to make the general point,
61	or does it make a point the canon doesn't?" Prune the first; keep the second.
62	
63	## A canon check covers an item too — and more strongly than prose
64	
65	The canon carries rules as **conformance checks**, not only prose. A local item is covered when a canon check
66	*enforces* it — stronger coverage than a stated line, since the rule runs on every session and CI pass.
67	Consult the machine-readable rule catalog (`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`:
68	id, severity, description, doc pointer — it lists the active local packs' own checks too) alongside the prose
69	corpus, and when a check covers the item, **quote the rule id** where you'd otherwise quote a canon line. This
70	cuts both ways: a **local pack's own check** is redundant once a canon check enforces the same rule — prune the
71	local `.mjs` (and drop it from `pack.mjs` + its fixture) exactly as you'd prune a duplicated prose line. The
72	keep-test above is unchanged: a local item that says *more* than the check detects (a stronger point about a
73	narrower case) stays.
74	
75	## Discipline
76	
77	- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon line (or the
78	  covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson.
79	- **Open a single PR against `main`** from a per-run-unique branch (see
80	  [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md)) — one PR for the
81	  whole run's prunes, not one per item — never a direct push. This is an unattended task, on a capable model, and a **wrongful prune
82	  deletes a real local lesson**, so — unlike [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md), whose additive edits
83	  ride a PR delivered to land after CI — this task keeps a **human** approval gate (its declared outcome ceiling
84	  is `open-pr`: it may open a PR but never merge it). **Put the issue reference in the commit message** —
85	  `Refs #<n>` for this task's tracking issue (below), in the commit itself, not only the PR body. The repo's
86	  `basics` `task-lifecycle` check gates a PR on its commits referencing an issue, so a prune commit that cites
87	  none reds the repo's CI and blocks the merge.
88	- If an edit touches something a test reads, run the repo's offline test suite and keep it green before pushing.
89	
90	## Tracking
91	
92	The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:
93	
94	> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Dedup**
95	
96	Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**. A run that finds no issue under

98	meaning, only the log does. Log each run that changed a doc as a **dated comment** — naming what was pruned and

100	
101	## Run on a capable model
102	
103	Proving the mounted canon genuinely covers a local item before pruning it — and telling "the canon now owns
104	this" from "the canon states this too generally, keep the local cut" — is a **judgment call**. A downgraded
105	model prunes a real lesson; the review PR is a backstop, but a wrongful prune is easy to wave through in

107

1	# Working in this repo
2	
3	The general lessons this repo has paid for once. The privacy boundary — the
4	product's defining constraint — has its own pack (`local/on-device-privacy`);
5	what follows is everything else.
6	
7	**Don't prune a `.gitignore` section in the same breath as deleting what it
8	ignored — the artifacts are still on disk.** Removing a toolchain (the Python
9	reference, a build system, a generator) invites tidying its ignore rules away in
10	the same commit, but the ignored artifacts it already produced are usually still
11	sitting untracked in the worktree — earlier test runs leave `__pycache__/`,
12	builds leave `build/`. The moment those rules go, the next `git add -A` sweeps
13	the artifacts *into* the very commit that was supposed to remove them, and
14	nothing complains: the commit is valid, the tests still pass, and the junk only
15	shows up as an inflated file count in the diff a reviewer reads. Delete the
16	artifacts from the worktree first (or `git clean` them), then drop their ignore
17	lines — and read `git diff --cached --stat` after any bulk `git add -A`, not just
18	`git status`, since staged additions are exactly what a clean `git status` stops
19	telling you about.
20	
21	**"Not statically checkable" is a verdict about the tree's shape at the time, not
22	about the rule — re-ask it after the tree changes.** `on-device-privacy`'s
23	"everything lives in one deletable directory" sat as prose because proving it
24	looked like it needed data-flow tracking of a `FileManager` write target back to
25	its declaration — true while the Python reference had many entry points, and
26	false the moment that tree went away: the native app has exactly two persistent
27	path roots, both the same search-path lookup, so constraining the *root*
28	constrains every path derived from it and no tracing is needed. A removal, a
29	migration, or a consolidation can collapse the entry points a rule has to cover,
30	so when a sweep meets prose a previous sweep left behind, re-derive the objection
31	against today's sources instead of trusting the recorded verdict.
32	
33	**"Already covered by another check" is a claim to test, not to reason out — hand
34	the sibling check a violating file before dropping a rule as a duplicate.** Three
35	sweeps in a row left `on-device-privacy`'s "the app listens on no socket" as
36	prose, each reasoning that an `NWListener` needs `import Network` and
37	`no-network-client` already bans that. True of that one API, false of the
38	capability: `socket(2)` comes free with `import Foundation` (Darwin is
39	re-exported), `NSXPCListener`/`CFSocket*`/`NSSocketPort` are Foundation types, and
40	an embedded HTTP server arrives as its own import — a file whose entire content
41	was `let fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0)` passed `check_the_world`
42	untouched. A ban list only covers the routes whoever wrote it thought of, so the
43	routes it misses are invisible to exactly the reasoning that drew it; running it
44	against a file that breaks the rule costs a minute and is the only step that can
45	disagree with you.
46	
47	**Write a check as a positive whitelist over an enumerated API surface, not as a
48	list of the bad cases.** `single-storage-directory` flags any search-path lookup
49	whose directory argument is not the literal `.applicationSupportDirectory`,
50	rather than enumerating the directories we don't want. Matching the allowed case
51	buys two things a ban list can't: a `SearchPathDirectory` case that doesn't exist
52	yet is caught the day it lands, and a non-literal argument (`urls(for: dir, in:)`)
53	becomes a finding too — indirection is precisely what would otherwise defeat the
54	check, so refusing to reason about it is a feature. Only invert this where the
55	allowed set is genuinely open-ended.
56	
57	**Ship a version the running app can state, and bump it whenever a build has to be
58	told apart from the last one.** Diagnosing the `installTap` crash (#61) stalled on
59	"which binary is installed?", and the answer had to be reconstructed by grepping a
60	crash report's symbol names for whether `finishListening` took a `generation:`
61	argument. Two causes, both durable. The menu header said only "LaughCounter"; and
62	several genuinely different builds all reported `0.2.1`, because the release
63	workflow keys its Release on `v<version>` read from `mac/Resources/Info.plist` — so
64	a merge that leaves `CFBundleShortVersionString` alone **refreshes the same
65	Release**, and the DMG behind the `latest/download` link changes identity without
66	changing its name. So the menu renders `LaughCounter v<version> (<build>)` from
67	`Bundle.main` rather than a constant in the source — `Info.plist` is already where
68	the version lives and where the release tag comes from, and a second copy could
69	disagree with the DMG it shipped in — and the **build number** is what separates
70	two builds that share a version string, so show it and raise it too. (#74/#75)
71	
72	**A scheduled job that *skips* its work still exits 0 — read what a green run says
73	it did.** This repo's Claudinite scheduler ran green every night while silently
74	skipping baselining, logging "no vendored mount (no stamp)" about a repo whose
75	`.claudinite-checks.json` carried one: the vendored `loadConfig` validated
76	`claudinite` as a legal settings key and then dropped it from the object it
77	returned, so the stamp read `undefined` and the run took the branch meant for a
78	pre-adoption repo. Nothing was red and nothing was missing — the only evidence was
79	one skip line in a log nobody opens on a green run. Two things follow. A *skip* is
80	a finding to read, not a pass: a job whose success and whose no-op look identical
81	from outside is telling you nothing. And when the bug lives inside the mechanism
82	that updates itself, the ordinary route is unreachable — baselining is what
83	refreshes the vendored mount, and the bug was *in* the mount — so the fix has to be
84	pushed in out of band rather than waited for. (#56)
85	
86	**Nothing in this repo runs on `pull_request`, so most PRs carry no checks at all
87	— and arming auto-merge on one is rejected every time.** `build-macos-dmg.yml`
88	and `release-macos-dmg.yml` trigger on `push` scoped to `mac/**` (plus their own
89	file), and `claudinite-scheduler.yml` only on `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch`; no
90	workflow here declares a `pull_request` trigger. A PR touching only
91	`.claudinite/`, `docs/` or `dev/` therefore starts nothing, is mergeable the
92	second it opens, and GitHub answers the auto-merge arm with *"already in clean
93	status — auto-merge only applies when checks are pending."* That is the repo's
94	shape, not a fault, and the canon's delivery procedure already licenses the
95	squash merge yourself in exactly that case — take it rather than escalating: PR
96	#138 sat unmerged for a day because a run read its task file's blanket "never
97	hand-merge" as covering the rejection too. Two corollaries. The maintenance PRs
98	the Action opens land **within seconds** of being armed, so by the time the agent
99	stage starts there is usually no open `claudinite/maintenance-*` PR left to
100	continue on and the condition that escalated no longer reproduces — three cycles
101	running (#127/#128, #129/#130, #133/#134) spent their budget hunting the PR API
102	for a branch that had already merged, when the first move is to fetch `main` and
103	re-run the check against it. And "CI will catch it" is simply false outside
104	`mac/**`: nothing runs, so whatever a change needed proving, prove it locally
105	before it lands. (#137/#138)
106	
107	**When a conformance check flags text, ask what a reader could act on before
108	reaching for an `accept`.** `claudinite-isolation` fired on `CLAUDE.md`'s
109	orientation header for spelling the vendored mount path. Nothing in that header
110	told a reader to go open the directory, so the path was pure decoration that
111	coupled a consumer file to a canon-internal layout — exactly the crossing the rule
112	exists to prevent, bought for nothing. Rewording to "vendored into this repo and
113	injected at session start" kept both facts a reader needs and lost only the
114	coupling. An `accept` entry is for a crossing that *must* exist; every one in this
115	repo's `.claudinite-checks.json` names a real constraint (a framework-fixed method
116	name, a deliberate broad-except, an optional-dependency availability probe). So
117	before adding one, delete the part the check is pointing at and see whether
118	anything actionable went with it — often nothing does. (#34)

1	# The microphone's lifecycle — an app that must never damage the device it uses
2	
3	LaughCounter holds a real microphone open for hours at a time, and the hardware
4	answers back: a USB webcam mic can be left **wedged** — dead system-wide, no
5	input meter anywhere, until it is physically re-plugged. Every rule here exists
6	because that happened, repeatedly, on the owner's Mac.
7	
8	The checks in this pack hold the three mechanical parts (only `AudioHub` builds
9	an engine; termination signals reach `applicationWillTerminate`; the app never
10	opts into sudden termination). What follows is the judgment half — the rules a
11	scan cannot decide. The **case history** — which release, which measurement,
12	which theory survived — lives in
13	[`dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md`](../../../../dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md)
14	and stays there; don't copy it here, read it before touching engine start/stop,
15	sleep/wake, exit handling, or `VoiceCommand`.
16	
17	**Never open the device to ask a question about it.** `AudioHub.makeEngine()`
18	touches `engine.inputNode`, and that property access opens the default input and
19	mints a hidden per-client aggregate device inside coreaudiod
20	(`CADefaultDeviceAggregate-<pid>-<n>`) — so a "cheap format read" in a retry
21	ladder is really a device open plus an aggregate create/destroy, measured at ~210
22	of them over 3h40m against hardware that was not there. Availability questions go
23	to `AudioDiagnostics`, which answers from `AudioObjectGetPropertyData` property
24	queries that open nothing. Cycling the device is the one mechanism by which this
25	app could plausibly damage it, so the cost of an answer is a property of the API
26	you ask, not of how often you ask.
27	
28	**Presence is not usability, at any layer.** `outputFormat(forBus: 0)` reports a
29	plausible 48 kHz with the input torn down while `inputFormat` reports 0, so a
30	guard written against the wrong one waves through starts that cannot succeed
31	(`AudioHub.validatedFormat()` requires both, and requires them to agree). One
32	layer down, a device can be enumerated and `alive=y` with a zero sample rate and
33	an unreadable name mid-teardown — so `AudioDiagnostics.hasUsableInput` demands a
34	nonzero rate and a sane channel count, not mere presence. Any new probe inherits
35	this: whatever it reads, ask what that field says while the mic is absent.
36	
37	**A duration is a claim about a span you observed.** "It has been present for N
38	seconds" is only as good as the watching behind it, and the sampling timer does
39	not fire while the Mac sleeps — which is why the settle gate was inert on exactly
40	the wake path it was built for (#107). Hence `inputAvailability` distinguishes
41	`.absent` from `.unobserved`, `noteObservationInterrupted()` is called from
42	`willSleep` so a sleep is declared rather than inferred, and the run is keyed on
43	the device's UID so a swap counts as a new arrival. Any future "X has been true
44	for N seconds" state gets the same three questions: was I watching, is it the
45	same device, and what does a gap in observation do to the claim?
46	
47	**Pick the clock by whether the span may contain a sleep.** `systemUptime` for
48	"how long has the stream been silent *while we were awake*" (buffer accounting,
49	stall windows); `Date()` for anything that can span a sleep — the sleep-duration
50	stamp in `AppDelegate` and the elapsed-time interruption backstop in
51	`AudioDiagnostics`. Both directions are wrong the other way round, and each site
52	in the sources says which it is and why.
53	
54	**Deferred work must be generation-guarded.** `asyncAfter` timers scheduled
55	before a sleep fire *immediately* on wake, so a delayed start that a stop raced
56	with would re-acquire the mic going into sleep or un-settled at wake. Every
57	intentional stop bumps `restartGeneration`; every delayed closure captures it and
58	aborts if it moved. When cancelling in-flight restarts, reset
59	`restartInFlight` / `restartQueued` / `suppressConfigChange` too, or the latches
60	stay stuck and block all future starts. Coalesce the wake fan-in with an **id**,
61	not a bool — a bool deadlocks when a re-sleep lands during the delay.
62	
63	**Never claim to be listening on the strength of `engine.start()` returning.**
64	That is what let the menu bar say 😄 *listening* through an entire evening of a
65	dead device, and it is why both wedge investigations had to be reconstructed from
66	logs instead of noticed. State shown to the user is derived from
67	`AudioDiagnostics.health` (`ok` / `stalled` / `noSignal`) — measured buffers —
68	and when a state has exactly one known remedy the UI names *that* remedy
69	(no-signal says unplug the mic; "Restart listening" is measured not to work).
70	
71	**Compile-green is not a gate for this code.** CI runs `swift build` and nothing
72	else, and every raise-vs-throw bug in this area is invisible to the compiler and
73	reachable in the first second of a run — two crash-on-launch builds shipped past
74	it. A change to `AudioHub`, the restart machinery, or the sleep/wake path is not
75	verified until it has actually started on a Mac. Reproduce the interesting case
76	without waiting for hardware to misbehave: let the display sleep, and coreaudiod
77	tears its contexts down seconds later.
78	
79	**Assume no toolchain on the machine that runs it.** The owner's Mac installs the
80	DMG from CI and has no Xcode command line tools, so anything needed to diagnose a
81	live failure is either shell built into macOS or compiled into the app by CI —
82	that is why the HAL reads live in `AudioDiagnostics` rather than in a helper
83	script. `command -v swift` does **not** test for a toolchain (`/usr/bin/swift` is
84	a stub that prompts for an 8 GB install); gate on `xcode-select -p` instead.
85

1	# macos-audio
2	
3	Holding a macOS microphone without damaging it. LaughCounter keeps an
4	`AVAudioEngine` input tap open for hours, and has repeatedly left a USB webcam mic
5	**wedged** — dead system-wide, no input meter anywhere, until physically
6	re-plugged. The rules distilled here come from that: `mac/Sources/LaughCounter/`
7	(`AudioHub`, `AudioDiagnostics`, `AppDelegate`'s restart machinery, `main.swift`),
8	`mac/Resources/Info.plist`, and the case history in
9	[`dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md`](../../../../dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md).
10	
11	A distinct technology domain — CoreAudio/AVFoundation device lifecycle — that no
12	canon pack homes, and that the repo's other local packs deliberately don't own:
13	`local/on-device-privacy` owns the privacy boundary, `local/laughcounter` the
14	repo's general build/packaging and check-authoring lessons.
15	
16	Local pack, declared by hand as `local/macos-audio` (no fingerprint).
17	
18	| Rule | How enforced |
19	| --- | --- |
20	| Only `AudioHub` builds an `AVAudioEngine` | `engine-construction-confined` check (`mac/Sources/**.swift`) |
21	| Termination signals reach `applicationWillTerminate`, `SIG_IGN` before `resume()` | `signal-teardown-routing` check (`mac/Sources/**.swift`) |
22	| Never opt into sudden termination | `no-sudden-termination` check (`mac/Resources/*.plist`) |
23	| Never open the device to ask a question about it | `RULES.md` prose |
24	| Presence is not usability, at any layer | `RULES.md` prose |
25	| A duration is only as good as the observation behind it | `RULES.md` prose |
26	| Pick the clock by whether the span may contain a sleep | `RULES.md` prose |
27	| Deferred work must be generation-guarded | `RULES.md` prose |
28	| Never claim "listening" on `engine.start()` returning | `RULES.md` prose |
29	| Compile-green is not a gate for this code | `RULES.md` prose |
30	| Assume no toolchain on the machine that runs it | `RULES.md` prose |
31	
32	The narrative — which release, which measurement, which theory survived — stays in
33	`dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md` rather than being copied here; `RULES.md`
34	carries the invariants and points at it.
35	
36	Fixtures: `pack.test.mjs` —
37	`node --test .claudinite/local/packs/macos-audio/pack.test.mjs`. Each
38	check has a violating fixture it fires on and the repo's real files it stays quiet
39	on. They sit in the pack, not alongside the app sources (`claudinite-isolation`).
40

1	# On-device privacy — the boundary the whole product is built around
2	
3	An always-on microphone in someone's living room only earns its place if what it
4	hears stays on the machine. That promise is the product requirement
5	(`docs/DESIGN-AND-TRADEOFFS.md` §0/§6, README *Privacy*), the text of the mic and
6	speech prompts users actually see (`mac/Resources/Info.plist`), and the reason
7	several design choices look heavier than they need to. The checks in this pack
8	hold the mechanical half; what follows is the judgment half.
9	
10	There is now exactly one implementation — the native app in `mac/Sources/` — so
11	every rule below is about it.
12	
13	**What may cross the boundary: derived metadata, never audio.** A laugh is
14	persisted as time, duration, confidence, and an origin label — that is what the
15	JSONL lines carry, and `LaughStore` says so in its own header. **No audio is
16	stored at all** — the `no-audio-persistence` check holds this mechanically for
17	v1. A feature that wants to keep audio (the v3 roadmap's rolling buffer) changes
18	the mic prompt and this check together, in the same PR.
19	
20	**Everything lives in one deletable directory.**
21	`~/Library/Application Support/LaughCounter/` holds the laugh log and the app's
22	own diagnostic log — the `single-storage-directory` check holds this mechanically,
23	by allowing `.applicationSupportDirectory` and nothing else as a search-path root.
24	The one path macOS dictates, not us, is a Login Item registration, which names no
25	directory of its own.
26	
27	**There is no accepted egress — none.** Detection (Sound Analysis) and speech
28	recognition (`SFSpeechRecognizer` with on-device recognition required) are both
29	built into macOS; no model is downloaded, no telemetry is sent, and the app makes
30	no outbound connection of any kind. The `no-network-client` check is therefore
31	absolute rather than carve-out-shaped. Adding *any* egress — a model fetch, a
32	crash reporter, a sync feature — is a product decision that gets written here and
33	in the README *Privacy* section before a line of it is written in Swift.
34	
35	**The disclosure must stay true.** `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` and
36	`NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` tell the user audio is analysed on-device
37	and not recorded.
38

1	# on-device-privacy
2	
3	LaughCounter's defining constraint as a local pack: an always-on living-room microphone whose audio
4	never leaves the machine. Distilled from this repo's own sources and requirements
5	(`docs/DESIGN-AND-TRADEOFFS.md` §0/§6, the README *Privacy* section,
6	`mac/Sources/LaughCounter/`) — the promise was stated in three docs and enforced nowhere.
7	
8	Local pack, declared by hand as `local/on-device-privacy` (no fingerprint). It covers the native
9	app, which since the Python reference was removed is the only implementation.
10	
11	| Rule | How enforced |
12	| --- | --- |
13	| No outbound client in capture path | `no-network-client` check (`mac/Sources/**.swift`) |
14	| Speech recognition on-device | `on-device-speech` check (`SFSpeechAudioBufferRecognitionRequest`) |
15	| Metadata persists, audio doesn't | `no-audio-persistence` check (`AVAudioFile`/`AVAudioRecorder`/`ExtAudioFileCreateWithURL`/`AudioFileCreateWithURL`) |
16	| One deletable directory | `single-storage-directory` check (only `.applicationSupportDirectory` as a search-path root) |
17	| No server / listener | `no-listener` check (`NWListener`/`NSXPCListener`/`CFSocket*`/`SocketPort`/`socket(2)`/an embedded HTTP-server import) |
18	| No egress at all | `RULES.md` prose |
19	| Usage strings stay true | `RULES.md` prose |
20	
21	Fixtures: `pack.test.mjs` — `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/on-device-privacy/pack.test.mjs`.
22	Each check has a violating fixture it fires on and the repo's real files it stays quiet on. They sit
23	in the pack, not alongside the app sources (`claudinite-isolation`).

1	# Extracting lessons — the bar and the local promotion ladder
2	
3	> **Scope: what both extraction skills share.** This doc is the **bar** a lesson must clear and the
4	> **ladder** it descends once it clears it — the half that is identical whatever the lesson was mined
5	> from. What each *source* adds is owned by its own skill:
6	> [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) for commits, merged PRs and issue
7	> activity, and [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) for a session's
8	> dialogue. Both load this doc; neither restates it.
9	
10	Its callers are the growth pack's [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md) daily task, which runs
11	both skills over one window, and an owner's occasional plain-words ask for a retrospective.
12	
13	## Run the pass on a capable model
14	
15	Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails
16	silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong "lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
17	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model to the judgment it
18	must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the separate efficiency analysis — also
19	live there; this doc is the how-to.
20	
21	## From signal to lesson — the bar
22	
23	A signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one
24	session or window.** Before adding anything:
25	
26	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded differently,
27	  even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
28	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or something already
29	  implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
30	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared, cross-project
31	  canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote stage lifts it there
32	  centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever travels.
33	
34	## Route to the local pack that owns it — the promotion ladder
35	
36	A project's capture surface is its **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/`); everything else
37	under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mounted canon and is never a capture target. Pick the pack whose
38	territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack; some segregate a domain pack), then
39	prefer the strongest mechanism it allows:
40	
41	1. **A check** in that pack's rules — author the `.mjs`, list it on the pack's `pack.mjs`, ship it with a
42	   red-first fixture. Its failure message *is* the lesson.
43	2. **A pack skill**, when the lesson is an activity-scoped procedure rather than a condition.
44	3. **Terse prose** in the pack's `RULES.md` — only what neither of the above can carry.
45	
46	Write **more checks and less prose**: a check relieves every session's context completely, where prose only
47	relocates it. When no pack's scope fits and the lesson warrants segregation, a new local pack is a
48	self-contained directory drop.
49	
50	**A gotcha tied to one call site is not a pack rule at all.** A trap from misusing a specific API, class, or
51	library goes as a **comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where the next editor of
52	that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list. Co-locate it in a file's own header
53	comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a
54	central gotchas doc for what no single usage site owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant
55	file (a mistake of omission), or a cross-cutting invariant.
56	
57	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
58	
59	Most sessions and most windows yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write
60	nothing rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes the
61	canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a genuinely new,
62	reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.
63

1	# claude-code-web-users-support — for the people working on this from the web
2	
3	A Claude Code **web** session runs for a signed-in person, in a managed container. A
4	terminal session does neither. This pack is where the capabilities that depend on that
5	difference live — anything a project can offer only when the session knows **who** is
6	here.
7	
8	## Personal interaction preferences
9	
10	This project reads each person's **personal interaction preferences** at session start:
11	how they want to be worked with — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, the
12	phrases they use to trigger a defined command. If the current user has a file in the
13	store, its contents are already in this session's context, injected under this pack's
14	marker by [`session-start.mjs`](session-start.mjs).
15	
16	**They are not project conventions.** Conventions belong to the packs that own each
17	subject and load as prose. What this carries is *personal*: the same rules travel with
18	a person across every project they work in, and two people on one project can want
19	different things. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project
20	convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the preference owns only the
21	trigger phrase.
22	
23	**The pack holds an address, not the content.** Preferences belong to a group of people
24	rather than to any one repository, so this project's declaration names the **store** —
25	a repo, and a path inside it holding one `<email>.md` per person:
26	
27	```json
28	{ "id": "claude-code-web-users-support", "config": { "repo": "owner/name", "path": "preferences" } }
29	```
30	
31	`path` is optional and defaults to `preferences`. Reading is **local-first**: when this
32	repo *is* the store, the working copy wins over the default branch, so an edit in
33	progress is what the session sees.
34	
35	**Every miss is fail-soft.** No identity (a terminal session has none), no configured
36	store, no file for this person, a fetch that fails — each is one plain-text note and the
37	session proceeds on default interaction behavior. Nothing here is load-bearing, and a
38	nice-to-have must never be able to stop a session from starting.
39	
40	### Adding or changing a preference
41	
42	Edit that person's file **in the store repo** — never here, and never in the canon. One
43	distilled preference per bullet, in the imperative: a preference is a rule the assistant
44	can act on, not a description of a mood. A preference that turns out to be a project
45	convention in disguise belongs in the pack that owns its subject instead.
46

1	# grow_with_claudinite
2	
3	Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
4	lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
5	Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the
6	existing fleet), and **opt-out by removal**: baselining never re-adds it.
7	
8	This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
9	lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
10	**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
11	that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.
12	
13	Its scheduled work is four tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
14	scheduler (`engine/scheduler/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:
15	
16	| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window, or a log is past retention | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI, plus the prune on the logs branch |
19	| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | weekly, when the canon or the project's local packs moved in the week | a PR against the repo's `main` |
20	| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via a reviewed PR |
21	| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | weekly (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |
22	
23	(Plus [usage-fold](tasks/usage-fold/task.md), the agentless daily fold described below.)
24	
25	## Extraction is one task over two sources
26	
27	`growth-extract` is the whole capture stage, and it runs **three skills** in order:
28	
29	1. [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) over the window's commits, merged
30	   PRs and issue discussion;
31	2. [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) over the logs captured
32	   from working sessions (plus the retention prune);
33	3. [prose-to-checks](skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) over the prose **that run just wrote**, to see
34	   whether any of it upgrades to a check before the PR opens.
35	
36	Everything lands in **one** PR, delivered to land where the repo's delivery settings allow
37	(`engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md`). The two extraction halves used to be two tasks firing in
38	the same nightly slot against the same local packs; they share the lesson bar, the promotion ladder
39	and the dedup surface ([extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)), so the split bought nothing
40	and cost a second opus dispatch, a second PR, and two runs deduping against a corpus the other was
41	concurrently writing.
42	
43	The third step is why the standing `prose-to-checks-sweep` is **weekly**: fresh prose is already
44	offered a conversion the night it is written, so what the sweep sees is a backlog that moves on a
45	weekly clock.
46	
47	A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
48	promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "grow_with_claudinite", "config": { "promote": false } }`
49	— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).
50	
51	## The conversation lifecycle — capture in-session, extract in the daily task, retention
52	
53	The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions**, replacing the old in-session post-merge
54	lessons pass. Capture and extraction split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session
55	transcript, so it runs in-session (at merge, and again when the session ends); **extraction** only
56	reads the already-pushed logs, so it is the conversation half of the ordinary `growth-extract`
57	scheduled task — the logs branch is *in the repo*, so reading it, committing lessons to local packs,
58	and pruning are plain local git on the working tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the
59	GitHub MCP tools.
60	
61	1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
62	   Right after a merge lands:
63	   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
64	   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
65	   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
66	   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
67	   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
68	   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
69	   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
70	   net), and pushes one file per **capture event** onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`**
71	   branch: `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`.
72	   **Delta-aware, keyed on the session id:** every capture pushes only the entries after this
73	   session's previous capture, whatever event produced it, so any two events chain into
74	   disjoint files and a zero delta pushes nothing at all. Double-writing is therefore safe by
75	   construction, not by coordination — the property [`session-end.mjs`](session-end.mjs) relies
76	   on, so `pack.test.mjs` pins it directly.
77	   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
78	   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
79	1. **Capture — again, when the session ends** ([session-end.mjs](session-end.mjs), invoked by the
80	   engine's SessionEnd hook runner for every active pack that ships one). Same capture, with
81	   `--issue 0`: **`0` means "no associated issue"**, and the filename shape stays byte-identical
82	   on purpose — the retention prune, the `conversationLogs` signal and the extract's filename
83	   parse all already accept it, whereas a *new* shape would be invisible to the prune and become
84	   immortal on the branch. This event is what captures the sessions that never merge (a review, an
85	   investigation, a session that ended in a question) and the post-merge **tail** of the ones that
86	   do. **Best effort:** a container reclaimed by timeout never fires it, so nothing depends on it
87	   having run — every firing enriches the record, every miss leaves exactly the merge-only
88	   behaviour. An `issue-0` log has no issue for the extract to post its exchange
89	   summary on; nothing else about its lifecycle differs.
90	   **Unattended sessions capture through the same step, deliberately not through the hook.** A
91	   scheduled task's executor session ends by having its container reclaimed, which is exactly
92	   the ending no `SessionEnd` fires on — so the executor runs the engine's runner itself as its
93	   last step and names its dispatch issue in `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE`, which this step uses in
94	   place of `0`. Those logs therefore file under the task that ran (the dispatch issue's title
95	   names `pack/task`), and the work no human watched becomes as countable as the work one did.
96	2. **Fresh pass — the conversation half of [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)**
97	   (precondition: a substantive merge, or a log actually past retention so the age-based prune still
98	   runs on a quiet repo; local git on the repo's working tree, MCP only for the issue comment). It
99	   applies the [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) skill (the
100	   friction signals and the measured efficiency analysis, computable from the log's timestamps and
101	   token usage) over [extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)'s shared bar, routes keepers into
102	   the member's local packs, and posts on the worked issue, for each rule that landed, a
103	   **200-word-max** summary of the slice of conversation that caused it — the dialogue itself is
104	   never pasted there, it is far too verbose for an issue —
105	   **extraction is the only path to permanence**: a log that yields no rule gets no comment,
106	   and its conversation is gone once retention deletes it (a deliberate owner call).
107	3. **Final pass and deletion** — once a log ages past `config.retention_days`, the same task
108	   re-reads it with ~a week of hindsight (the rethink window), then deletes it (the age-based
109	   precondition arm guarantees the prune runs even on a repo gone quiet). Every log gets exactly two
110	   judgment passes. **Unset retention = the prune deletes nothing** (capture-only, fail-safe).
111	
112	No adoption question over it — `retention_days` stays unset (hidden) by default, which is
113	fail-safe (capture-only). A project that wants the prune active sets `config.retention_days`
114	itself (10 is the recommended floor); nothing else to schedule, since extraction rides the
115	fleet's one daily run like the other growth tasks.
116	
117	## Skill-usage metrics — what the mounted skills actually do
118	
119	Mounting a skill only puts its name and one-line description into the session prompt; whether the
120	model ever **loads** it is discretion, and nothing recorded it. So the promotion ladder's
121	skill-vs-prose call had no empirical feedback: a skill whose trigger never fires looked exactly like
122	one that fires daily, and a "skill" that loads in every session (rules wearing a skill's clothes)
123	looked exactly like a genuinely activity-scoped one.
124	
125	The [usage-fold](tasks/usage-fold/task.md) task closes that loop — daily, agentless, seconds. It
126	counts skill loads **and their denominators** (captures, merges, sessions, user messages, user
127	commands) out of the logs this pack already captures, into
128	`.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`: day rows recomputed statelessly inside the raw retention
129	window, week rows appended once past a `foldedThrough` watermark. Denominators are the point — a raw
130	count cannot tell healthy-rare from broken, so the question is loads *against the sessions where that
131	skill's own declared trigger plausibly applied*. Zeros are implicit (a skill with no loads has no
132	key), which is what makes "never loads" visible: diff the file against the repo's mounted skills.
133	
134	Fleet-wide aggregation is deliberately **not** here — the canon knows mechanisms, never repos. It is
135	the sheepdog pack's [`fleet-usage`](../sheepdog/tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) task, in the fleet-enforcer
136	repo, which is the only place that knows who the members are.
137	
138	## Rules
139	
140	| Rule | Kind | What |
141	|---|---|---|
142	| `growth-config` | hardcoded ([config-check.mjs](config-check.mjs)) | entry config shape valid |
143	
144	**Pack discovery** ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) is
145	an ordinary weekly task on the repo's own scheduler. The repo runs the whole pipeline over
146	**itself**: manifest its stack, hold it against the canon packs already on its shelf and its own
147	existing local packs, and — for genuinely project-specific knowledge neither homes — author a new
148	**local** pack populated from its real usage, landed through a **reviewed** PR (a new pack ships new
149	`.mjs` checks, and a check can break CI — the same reason `prose-to-checks-sweep` is reviewed, and
150	the one place this stage differs from extract). It writes only the repo's own
151	`.claudinite/local/packs/`; lifting a local pack up into the shared canon is the central promote
152	task's job.
153	
154	## Identifying a project's capture surface: its local packs (the same way in every stage)
155	
156	Every growth stage operates on a project's **local packs** — the tracked packs a repo keeps under
157	`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/` (prose in `RULES.md`, checks in the pack's `rules`, activity
158	procedures as the pack's skills, scheduled tasks under its `tasks/`). That subtree **is** the
159	project's own content;
160	the rest of `.claudinite/` is the **read-only mounted canon** and is never a capture, prune, or
161	promote target. So "a project's local packs" means precisely *everything under
162	`.claudinite/local_packs/`, and nothing else under `.claudinite/`*. This is the normalized capture
163	surface — a structural set the stages read the same way, not a `CLAUDE.md`-graph walk over stray
164	Markdown (a repo with no local packs yet simply has nothing to extract, dedup, or promote here; a
165	project adopts the structure via the `generate-project-instructions` skill).
166	
167	Prefer the strongest mechanism the lesson allows — the **local promotion ladder**, applied at the
168	project's own level: a deterministic rule becomes a **check** in the owning pack's `rules` (its
169	failure message carries the lesson), an activity-scoped procedure becomes a **pack skill**, and only
170	what neither can carry lands as **prose** in a pack's `RULES.md`. A check relieves every session's
171	context completely where prose only relocates it, so capture writes *more checks and less prose*.
172	
173	The stages differ only in *how they read that set*, never in *which set it is*: extract and dedup
174	run against the member repo and read the local packs from the working tree; promote runs centrally
175	and reads the same subtree over the GitHub API (get-file-contents under `.claudinite/local_packs/`).
176	Extract writes into it, promote reads from it, dedup prunes within it — all against the identical,
177	`.claudinite/local_packs/`-rooted set.
