input.title: growth-dedup: prune local items now covered by canon
input.head: growth-dedup-149-1786251446
input.body:
Weekly growth-dedup run. Context named these four canon packs as the yardstick for this run (dispatch issue #149): `claude-code-web-users-support`, `basics`, `grow_with_claudinite`, `github-actions`. Every local pack under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (`laughcounter`, `macos-audio`, `on-device-privacy`) was checked against them. Two items were **stripped**; nothing else overlapped these four packs closely enough to prune with confidence — when unsure, the item was left alone.

## Stripped

### `.claudinite/local/packs/laughcounter/RULES.md` — the "nothing runs on `pull_request`" lesson

The lesson's middle clause read:

> That is the repo's shape, not a fault, **and the canon's delivery procedure already licenses the squash merge yourself in exactly that case — take it rather than escalating**: PR #138 sat unmerged for a day...

`grow_with_claudinite`'s `unattended-agents` skill now states this generally:

> "Where a shared delivery procedure exists (Claudinite's `engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md`), the merges it licenses — **like the direct merge on a base branch that requires nothing, where the arm is rejected 'clean status' by design** — are the sanctioned path, not a workaround; anything outside them stays unlanded."
> — `.claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`

That's exactly LaughCounter's rejected-arm scenario, generalized. Stripped the now-canon-owned clause; kept the residue — this repo's own workflow shape (no `pull_request` trigger anywhere), the PR #138 incident (a run misread its own task file's blanket "never hand-merge" as covering this too), and the corollaries about maintenance-PR timing and "CI won't catch it outside `mac/**`" — none of which the canon states.

### `.claudinite/local/packs/on-device-privacy/RULES.md` — "The disclosure must stay true"

The paragraph read:

> **The disclosure must stay true.** `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` and `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` tell the user audio is analysed on-device and not recorded.

`basics/RULES.md` now states the general rule this leans on this repo's two usage-string names to make:

> "A user-facing statement about what the software does with a user's data — a permission prompt's usage string, a privacy policy, a store-listing disclosure — is part of the behaviour's contract, not documentation of it. Change the behaviour and the statement changes in the same commit; a stale disclosure is worse than a blunt one. And read the direction the other way too: retaining something previously not retained, adding an outbound connection, or opening a listener is a change to the promise, not a new field — it earns an explicit decision, and the disclosure rewrite, before the code."
> — `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/RULES.md`

Stripped the now-canon-owned lead sentence ("The disclosure must stay true"); kept the residue — which two strings exist and what they currently promise (on-device, not recorded), since that's project-specific content the general canon rule has no way to carry.

## Not pruned

`macos-audio` and `on-device-privacy`'s remaining items are all CoreAudio/AVFoundation device-lifecycle or on-device-speech/privacy specifics that none of the four named canon packs address. `laughcounter`'s other six lessons (`.gitignore`-vs-artifacts sequencing, "not statically checkable" being tree-shape-dependent, testing a sibling check before trusting it as duplicate coverage, positive-whitelist check authorship, version/build-number identity, and "a green scheduled run can still have silently skipped its work") each make a point the four named packs don't state generally — left unchanged.

## Verification

- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — clean (exit 0)
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — clean (exit 0), including `dedup-prune-integrity` and `task-lifecycle`
- `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/macos-audio/pack.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/on-device-privacy/pack.test.mjs` — 23/23 pass

Refs #149. Per the growth-dedup task's outcome ceiling (`open-pr`), this PR is **not** merged by the agent — human approval required.

{"number":157,"title":"growth-dedup: prune local items now covered by canon","body":"Weekly growth-dedup run. Context named these four canon packs as the yardstick for this run (dispatch issue #149): `claude-code-web-users-support`, `basics`, `grow_with_claudinite`, `github-actions`. Every local pack under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (`laughcounter`, `macos-audio`, `on-device-privacy`) was checked against them. Two items were **stripped**; nothing else overlapped these four packs closely enough to prune with confidence — when unsure, the item was left alone.

## Stripped

### `.claudinite/local/packs/laughcounter/RULES.md` — the "nothing runs on `pull_request`" lesson

The lesson's middle clause read:

> That is the repo's shape, not a fault, **and the canon's delivery procedure already licenses the squash merge yourself in exactly that case — take it rather than escalating**: PR #138 sat unmerged for a day...

`grow_with_claudinite`'s `unattended-agents` skill now states this generally:

> "Where a shared delivery procedure exists (Claudinite's `engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md`), the merges it licenses — **like the direct merge on a base branch that requires nothing, where the arm is rejected 'clean status' by design** — are the sanctioned path, not a workaround; anything outside them stays unlanded."
> — `.claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`

That's exactly LaughCounter's rejected-arm scenario, generalized. Stripped the now-canon-owned clause; kept the residue — this repo's own workflow shape (no `pull_request` trigger anywhere), the PR #138 incident (a run misread its own task file's blanket "never hand-merge" as covering this too), and the corollaries about maintenance-PR timing and "CI won't catch it outside `mac/**`" — none of which the canon states.

### `.claudinite/local/packs/on-device-privacy/RULES.md` — "The disclosure must stay true"

The paragraph read:

> **The disclosure must stay true.** `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` and `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` tell the user audio is analysed on-device and not recorded.

`basics/RULES.md` now states the general rule this leans on this repo's two usage-string names to make:

> "A user-facing statement about what the software does with a user's data — a permission prompt's usage string, a privacy policy, a store-listing disclosure — is part of the behaviour's contract, not documentation of it. Change the behaviour and the statement changes in the same commit; a stale disclosure is worse than a blunt one. And read the direction the other way too: retaining something previously not retained, adding an outbound connection, or opening a listener is a change to the promise, not a new field — it earns an explicit decision, and the disclosure rewrite, before the code."
> — `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/RULES.md`

Stripped the now-canon-owned lead sentence ("The disclosure must stay true"); kept the residue — which two strings exist and what they currently promise (on-device, not recorded), since that's project-specific content the general canon rule has no way to carry.

## Not pruned

`macos-audio` and `on-device-privacy`'s remaining items are all CoreAudio/AVFoundation device-lifecycle or on-device-speech/privacy specifics that none of the four named canon packs address. `laughcounter`'s other six lessons (`.gitignore`-vs-artifacts sequencing, "not statically checkable" being tree-shape-dependent, testing a sibling check before trusting it as duplicate coverage, positive-whitelist check authorship, version/build-number identity, and "a green scheduled run can still have silently skipped its work") each make a point the four named packs don't state generally — left unchanged.
